items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled lemma at source lines 1330-1333, original Lemma 8.5.5: on a connected H-space both translations mu(a,-) and mu(-,a) are equivalences. The author's proof (source lines 1335-1354) is not a direct computation but a descent argument: the statement that a translation is an equivalence is a proposition-valued family, so proving it means producing a section (lines 1339-1341), and since the universe of propositions is a set the family descends along 0-truncation to a family on trunc 0 A (lines 1343-1344). Connectedness makes trunc 0 A contractible, so it suffices to inhabit the fiber at the basepoint, where the unit law of the H-space identifies the translation with the identity (lines 1345-1349). The last two lines transfer the result back along the truncation. The statement gives no hint that the argument goes through truncation and contractibility.
